column1: # Lunate verify shard weights - the recorded wall time of ONE culture pass of each `lunate.slnx`
# test project, in seconds, plus the `#primary` row: the wall time shard 1 spends on its non-test
# steps (tools, build, publish, startup budget, install/tool/extension roundtrips, the two
# Category=Perf budgets). scripts/test-parallel.sh reads this file and nothing else to partition the
# test phase: one unit per test project, both culture passes together, placed largest recorded weight
# first into the least-loaded shard. The process-bound half of the Coding suite is its own project,
# Lunate.Coding.Process.Tests, so a shard never carries the whole slow suite (#789).
# A project with no row here is partitioned at the default weight (VERIFY_SHARD_DEFAULT_WEIGHT), so
# adding a test project does not fail the gate; a row naming a project lunate.slnx no longer has fails
# scripts/gate-tests.sh, so a rename or a deletion is what asks for a refresh.
# Refresh from a real run's artifacts - the per-project records a gate run writes beside its shard
# Recorded from a real run's own per-project records: the four shards of
# `bash scripts/verify.sh --shard i/4` on 2026-11-28 (osx-arm64, macOS 26.3.1, Mac mini M4, 10 cores),
# each shard's default and de-AT pass recorded by scripts/shard-weights.sh and folded with
# `weights --from`, taking the slower of a project's two recorded passes. Before this run the table
# named one project and left the other twenty-two on the default weight, which is what the review
# sent back (#1043). The split's two Coding rows are the recorded suite's 406 s divided at the
# process boundary (300 + 116); the next run's records replace them.
# Known skew, recorded with the numbers rather than hidden: the lane sandbox blocks 19 process-tree
# and pty tests in the Coding suite (ProcessSession, BashBackgroundJob, ProcessRunner,
# UnixChildProcess, SignalTerminalRestore, DiagnosticScrubber, BashGuardTool and WaitDiagnosis tests),
# and their timeout waits are part of the suite's recorded 406 s. The split moves those tests into
# `Lunate.Coding.Process.Tests`, whose 116 s and `Lunate.Coding.Tests`' 300 s are the split above.
# The Windows lane's own record for one pass of the old suite is about 390 s. `#primary` is the
# reference run's 110 s: a full local gate run is not measurable on this machine (the sandbox kills
# it), and the same fold refreshes it from a run's `verify-<rid>-<shard>-of-<n>.json`.
